editorial.headline: Intellectual-Property Consultancy, and Bali’s PMA Divide
editorial.standfirst: This activity handles intellectual-property applications across a wide range of rights; it is nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, but PMA registration is blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 69103 covers the professional work of submitting and handling intellectual-property applications, together with related activity in the same field. Its scope reaches across patents, copyright, trademarks, geographical indications, industrial designs, integrated-circuit layout designs, trade secrets and other intellectual-property matters. The record also places intellectual-property consultancy offices and law offices within the activity. This is therefore a broad rights-administration practice, concerned with moving applications and related matters through their proper course.

The activity is open at every scale listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That range suits a field that can be carried out through an intellectual-property consultancy office or a law office, while still encompassing a substantial spread of intellectual-property subject matter. The scale categories establish that the activity is not confined to one size of operation; they do not alter what the activity itself covers, which remains the submission, handling and related work associated with intellectual-property matters.

Nationally, the position is straightforward. This activity is marked TERBUKA under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits PMA registration with foreign ownership up to that full ceiling. There is no national foreign-ownership cap below 100% to qualify in this case. That openness is material, but it is not the whole answer for a founder intending to establish the activity in Bali.

In Bali, the conclusion changes decisively: a foreign investor cannot register this activity through PMA today. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low on every scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s moratorium of May 13, 2026. The provincial rule blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, island-wide and permanently. The national ceiling of 100% remains the national figure; it does not override Bali’s PMA block. For a Bali proposal, the honest answer is a present bar on PMA registration.
